rows.subtype: Hiding behind a parent at a party [Actor]
rows.description: A child clings to a parent's leg and refuses to greet anyone; staying away from the scary thing feels like relief, and gentle nearness helps more than pushing.
The child complains of a stomach ache and stays home, and the fear drops at once. Relief teaches the brain that avoidance is the safe move, so next time the fear starts earlier.
A teenager delays a project because a poor result would reveal weakness; putting it off protects the self-image but makes the eventual work worse.
A child called lazy by parents for dawdling over homework starts to believe it as a fact about themself. Breaking the task into steps and sitting nearby for the start helps more than scolding.
A child who stumbles while reading makes a silly face and gets the class laughing with them; the joke keeps control of the moment, though constant clowning can hide worry.
A child learns idioms, hints and jokes, and asks what someone meant. Indirect speech may show politeness or humour, and asking what someone means is a good habit.
A child says a project will be quick and starts the night before. He imagines the ideal path and forgets past delays.

rows.subtype: Approach: estimates from the best case and expects to finish early [Pitfall]
rows.description: A student thinks a project will take three days if all goes well, and it takes ten with interruptions, a broken laptop and unclear steps.
A child who stumbles while reading makes a silly face and gets the class laughing with them; the joke keeps control of the moment, though constant clowning can hide worry.
A preschooler tells jokes that miss the punchline, uses nonsense words and giggles at silly rhymes. The child enjoys the pattern of humour before fully grasping why something is funny.
A child says a project will be quick and starts the night before. He imagines the ideal path and forgets past delays.

rows.subtopic: Estimating time and the planning fallacy
rows.description: A teenager estimates a project by imagining everything going smoothly and starts late as a result. The mind plans from the ideal story and ignores how similar tasks have actually gone before.
